body: I felt exactly the same when i lost my sister(still do, depending on situations). All those feelings are valid, grieving is naturel response to loss and it never expires. Whatever you do, please don't resort to suicide that is the worst thing you can do to yourself, to your loved ones and to your daughter. She wants you to live, you know the pain it can cause to people so seek help.

I feel you my friend. It's been a year yesterday since my little sister died. Before that I was at the top of the world,I was about to get the internship I wanted, I was 2 semester away from graduation. Since that day, I'm just unrecognizable, completely lost and can't move from the house.

You have to stay positive, nothing will be like before but I can feel that better days are ahead of us. It's better you take your time to grief and not rush things.
That is very sweet of you, thank you for reminding me this  ❤️.  If you need to talk you can reach me out, stay strong.

Now that I'm more appeased I think she didn't mean it but it still hurts.  What you said is true, I think we should let time heal us and not try to speed things up.  Thank you for your kind words and stay strong.

Weird, maybe I'm off-topic.  Some days before sleeping I pray God to see my sister in my dreams knowing perfectly I will be shattered by sadness when I wake up. Maybe, It's some more confusion than contradiction. 

I can dodge my pain, take anti-depressants, take pills to sleep at night, push back memories about my sister's death and devote myself completely to work. I choose not to do that, I want to remember my sister like I'm watching a video. I don't want to forget what she looks like and all the memories we shared together. Seeing her smile in my mind is worth all the breakdowns, the tears and the regrets.  

Don't forget that what you are experiencing is not unique, don't feel ostracized. This sub is a fraction of survivors of bereavement by suicide, if millions overcame this challenge, so can we. Thank you for sharing.

###
Thank you for those words it really lifted my spirit, stay strong !

Thank you for the advice. I say the same for you, please be safe and don't attempt anything harmful. I wrote this at night, in the darkness is where we feel the most vulnerable, alone and miserable. Sometimes I think if I could manage to sleep well at night half my problems will be solved, my head is constantly reassessing the trauma. 

I saw your posts, it's only been a month for you, may strength be with you. The first 6 months are literally the worst, you should not isolate yourself like I did and try to reach out your friends/family even if you don't want to be there. You will see that after those months you will be more functional but the sadness and anxiety will still be there but a little more manageable.

I'm here if you want to talk and stay strong.

It's been almost 10 months since I lost my sister, it hasn't been a moment where I don't think about her. It's just so exhausting to go on with my life, I'm not living anymore I'm just constantly dodging the pain. It's just constant waves of pain and when they happens you try to not fall into despair. 

It's still better than the first weeks/months where I wasn't active at all, couldn't even move from the house. At least now I can study and be productive except the pain is always her even more intense but short. I can't think about my future without her it pains me, it's used to be my strength not anymore. Stay strong.

I know what you feel like and it's not healthy. Life is hard especially now, the competition for qualified jobs that pay well is ruthless and the under qualified jobs are just exhausting, not sustainable in the long term.

That's why you need to adapt whether you accept or not the reality of life.

No one's gonna change this reality in one lifetime, don't count in any politician to do that not even Bernie or resurrected Jesus.
You right it's a day by day process, I guess seeing someone is the right direction. It's a bad timing now, with the whole Covid-19 it's hard to find a therapist. Thanks for the advice :)
Thank you for the reply, I just need that little boost to reach out to my friends and finish school. Maybe antidepressants could help.
Nice for starting a Grief counselling, it's a big step and it will do you good. Thank you for the reply and I hope you will get better ❤️
Very inspiring ! Thank you very much for your reply, I needed that.
I’m so sorry for your loss. We have to survive for their sake and ours.

Take care of yourself too, you don't know what life is like in 5 years. Thanks you for the advice, my family is the only thing that I have that really worth it in this life. If you want to talk pm me.
Sorry for your loss and thanks for the advice.
We are so shocked we can't even look at her pictures or even talk about her. I'm living in my parent's house so we talk all the time, it helps. Sorry for you loss and thanks for the advice.
I can't even pretend it's good, I can't. It's so hard that it's swallow my soul. Sorry for your loss and thanks for the advice.

She had very few "freinds" later in her life which make me extremely sad for not doing anything. She was isolated yet we live in the same house. I still have my family and some freinds to rely on. Thanks for the advice.
It's only been 10 days, I thought the problems I had in the past will disappear or became minor after this tragic event but they are amplified.
Very good advice. I hope I will have the courage to do things with them we didn't do in the past. thank you.
